newsitem.title: ROMANIA: First Romania results confirm opposition lead.
newsitem.headline: First Romania results confirm opposition lead.

text.p: Romania's anti-communist opposition has taken a strong lead in the Balkan country's parliamentary poll, first official results showed on Monday.

The Democratic Convention (CDR) was confirmed as strong enough to end seven years of government by ex-communists. But in the presidential race, CDR leader Emil Constantinescu trailed incumbent Ion Iliescu by three percent with a fifth of votes counted.

Figures for the presidential race, which will go to a second round of voting in two weeks time, showed Iliescu doing better than exit polls suggested, with 31.8 percent. Constantinescu won 28.5 percent support.
The official figures released by the Central Electoral Bureau put the CDR ahead in the lower Chamber of Deputies with 30.8 percent, compared to 20.8 percent for Iliescu's Party of Social Democracy.

Figures for the upper house, the Senate, were broadly similar. Ex-premier Petre Roman's Social Democratic Union was third with 13 percent in both chambers and looks set to hold the balance of power in any coalition government.

The ethnic Hungarian party ranked fourth with some six percent. Romanian nationalist parties look to be the only other political groups scoring strongly enough to beat the three percent threshold for a place in parliament.
